findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in the ADR/verdict-adapter how the agentic engine yields INDETERMINATE and fail-closes on a degraded run (timeout, budget exhaustion, malformed/partial output, provider unavailability), so a failed agent run never resolves to a signable PASS.

findings.finding: The verdict adapter under-specifies how the single-agent engine produces INDETERMINATE and its fail-closed behavior on a degraded run; the current engine derives INDETERMINATE from pipeline-internal states (llm_unavailable, verify_failed, hierarchy_incomplete, prerequisite_indeterminate) that a single structured-output agent has no analog for, so a truncated/malformed/budget-exhausted agent run could collapse to PASS and mint an attestation — violating the 'No bypass' invariant.

findings.suggested_fix: Define the agentic engine's coverage/outcome mapping: an agent run that does not complete with valid structured output sets llm_unavailable/verify_failed-equivalent coverage and resolves INDETERMINATE (never PASS); only a clean, completed run with zero blocker-severity findings reaches PASS.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the failure-disposition contract for the new-model API-rejection failures: whether a 400 from forced tool_choice / rejected sampling params / rejected prefill is fatal/non-retryable, and which disposition wins when both the Bedrock primary and the Anthropic fallback reject the same request (preserving a retryable primary throttle).
evidence: affects_failure_disposition = yes: the audit adds a new class of 400-rejection failures ('forced tool_choice any/tool returns a 400 on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5', 'temperature/top_p/top_k are rejected', 'assistant prefill is rejected') on a path that now routes through the existing Bedrock->Anthropic fallback.

disposition_contract_stated = no: the plan says to 'Check whether structured output relies on forced tool calls' and fix incompatibilities, but never states whether a new-model API-rejection 400 is treated as fatal/non-retryable vs retryable, nor which disposition wins if both Bedrock and the Anthropic fallback reject the same malformed request.

The 1c0d pattern applies: a non-retryable, permanently malformed request (400 on forced tool_choice) should not be masked as a retryable transient error by the fallback chain, and a retryable primary (e.g. a Bedrock 429) must not be masked by the fallback's own failure.
findings.finding: The model-call audit identifies NEW failure modes under Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 (forced tool_choice any/tool returns 400, temperature/top_p/top_k rejected, assistant prefill rejected), and the agentic engine reuses the existing Bedrock-first-with-Anthropic-fallback chain, but the plan never states the disposition of these new API-rejection failures nor the fallback-failure winner for them.
findings.location: Approach step 2 (model-call audit) and step 3 ('runs on rebar's existing LLM runtime and provider chain, so Bedrock-first with fallback still applies')
scenarios: A residual forced-tool_choice call survives the audit, Bedrock Opus 5.5 returns a 400, the chain falls back to Anthropic which also 400s, and the permanently-malformed request is surfaced (or retried) under the wrong disposition.
findings.suggested_fix: Record in the ADR/audit that a new-model API-rejection 400 is classified fatal/non-retryable (not a WAIT_AND_RETRY/exit-11 throttle) and that the Bedrock->Anthropic fallback preserves the most-recoverable leg — a retryable Bedrock 429 is never masked by the fallback's own non-retryable 400.

findings.finding: The parent's Same-certification invariant names pin-currency checks as an acceptor of the plan-review attestation ('accepted identically by the claim and close gates, review-plan --status, sign-review, and pin-currency checks'), and parent AC6 requires the engine-bearing attestation to be accepted by the certification path. Child 4cc4's acceptance criteria enumerate claim, close, review-plan --status and sign-review but omit pin-currency checks. No sibling in the roster names pin-currency. This is a partial-without-remainder: the uncovered remainder — that pin-currency checks accept the agentic attestation carrying the new engine field — is owned by no child.
scenarios: An agentic PASS attestation whose added signed `engine` field or back-compat default is read differently by the pin-currency path than by the claim/close gates, causing a currency check to reject or misclassify an attestation the gates accept.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion and test to child 4cc4 asserting the pin-currency check accepts both an agentic attestation carrying engine:"agentic" and a pre-existing attestation defaulting to "pipeline", matching the parent's Same-certification invariant.
